introduction.definition: A submerged hollow-fibre microfiltration system immerses cassettes of porous fibres directly in the feed tank. A permeate pump applies gentle suction so clean water passes into the fibres while suspended solids and bacteria stay outside. Air scouring and periodic back-pulsing keep the fibres clean.

video_tutorials.title: Microfiltration System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Microfiltration System.
A submerged hollow-fibre microfiltration system immerses cassettes of porous fibres directly in the feed tank.
A permeate pump applies gentle suction so clean water passes into the fibres while suspended solids and bacteria stay outside.
Air scouring and periodic back-pulsing keep the fibres clean.
Typical applications include membrane bioreactors (MBR) for wastewater; surface-water treatment; tertiary filtration.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Blower Impeller, Permeate Pump (reversible for backpulse), Permeate Pump (reversible for backpulse) — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Microfiltration System works.
Feed fills the membrane tank.
The permeate pump draws water into the fibres.
Solids are retained on the fibre surface.
The blower supplies air that scours the fibres.
Permeate leaves via the header.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The permeate pump applies a gentle suction inside the fibres (trans-membrane pressure typically only ~ 0.1–0.5 bar), drawing clean water in through the pores while solids stay outside.

video_tutorials.title: Microfiltration System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Microfiltration System.
Monitor TMP, flux and air flow.
Maintenance clean (hypochlorite/citric).
Recovery clean; fibre repair/replacement.
Watch for sludging of the cassette: rising TMP, clogged fibres. Common cause: low air scour, high solids.
Watch for fibre breakage: turbidity in permeate. Common cause: abrasive debris, poor screening.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
